x,y,w,h = roi

for name in ['bt_portal_merchant.png','bt_portal_leave.png']:
    t = cv2.imread('templates/'+name)
    print()
    print('===',name,'tpl',t.shape[1],'x',t.shape[0],'===')
    for label,search,ox,oy in (('ROI ',sub,x,y),('FULL',frame,0,0)):
        rows=[]
        for s in [round(v,2) for v in np.arange(0.50,1.55,0.05)]:
            tw,th = max(1,int(t.shape[1]*s)), max(1,int(t.shape[0]*s))
            if search.shape[0]<th or search.shape[1]<tw: continue
            ts = cv2.resize(t,(tw,th), interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA if s<1 else cv2.INTER_LINEAR)
            r = cv2.matchTemplate(search, ts, cv2.TM_CCOEFF_NORMED)
            _,mv,_,ml = cv2.minMaxLoc(r)
            rows.append((mv,s,ml[0]+ox+tw//2, ml[1]+oy+th//2))
        rows.sort(reverse=True)
        print(' ',label,'best5:')
        for mv,s,cx,cy in rows[:5]:
            print(f'      scale={s:.2f} score={mv:.3f} center=({cx},{cy})')
"

How a customer release actually ships, and the auth wall that cost an hour on 2026-05-30.

**TOKEN + ACCOUNT-ID - both env vars are now persisted (2026-06-02).** The R2:Edit token (`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, starts `cfut_`) AND `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID=[redacted-flag]` are now `setx`-persisted in the User registry, so a brand-new shell has them. TWO gotchas when using them: (1) the Claude PowerShell/Bash tool spawns a FRESH shell per call and does NOT reload registry env mid-session, and an OLD `wrangler login` OAuth token (no r2 scope) takes over when the env var is absent - so ALWAYS set `$env:CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN=...` (+ `$env:CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID=...`) INLINE in the same command that calls wrangler/build_lua_bundle. (2) The R2:Edit token alone makes `wrangler r2 object put` fail with `/memberships ... Authentication error [code: 10000]` (wrangler resolves the account via /memberships, which the token can't read) - setting `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` bypasses that lookup and the put succeeds. `r2 bucket list` works without it; `object put` does not. Don't add User-Details/Memberships perms to the token - just set the account-id env var.

**THE R2 AUTH GOTCHA (the big one):** the lua bundle is uploaded ONLY by `tools/build_lua_bundle.py` → `wrangler r2 object put abyss-bot-downloads/lua/<version>.zip`. **`wrangler login` (OAuth) does NOT grant R2** - its token scopes are `account/workers/d1/pages/queues/...` but never `r2`, so EVERY R2 call (even `wrangler r2 bucket list`) dies with `Authentication error [code: 10000]`. Re-logging in does not help; the account is `[redacted-flag]` and OAuth simply never carries R2. The upload works only when a **`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` with `Account → Workers R2 Storage → Edit`** is set in the shell (`$env:CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN=...`). It is NOT persisted anywhere on the machine (not in env User/Machine scope, not in any file, not in the PS profile) - so a fresh shell won't have it. Symptom that you're hitting this: `wrangler whoami` shows scopes with no `r2` line + "Unable to retrieve email" (token also lacks User Details:Read). Fix = create/set the API token; do NOT chase "wrong account" or re-login.

**Full release sequence (all needed; a lua-only change still needs ALL of it because version must match across exes + bundle):**
1. Bump `version.py` (single source of truth; embedded in exes + used as the lua bundle key + `__BOT_VERSION__` placeholder).
2. `py tools/build_lua_bundle.py` → uploads `lua/<version>.zip` (needs the R2 token above). See [[feedback_ship_checklist]].
3. PyInstaller rebuild BOTH `bot.spec` AND `tray.spec` (version mismatch = update loop, see [[feedback_pyinstaller_tray_stale]]); verify deps first ([[feedback_ship_deps_verify]]).
4. Build installer `abyss-bot-setup-<version>.exe`, compute sha256.
5. Swap `manifest.json` on `download.abyss.bot` (version + sha256 + url) - THIS is what triggers customer auto-update (updater.py polls `https://download.abyss.bot/manifest.json`). Also an R2 upload.
6. `git commit` (+ push - but NOTE: this repo had NO git remote/upstream configured as of 2026-05-30).

**MANUAL "Check for updates" tray button was BROKEN until 0.5.43 (fixed 2026-06-24).** `tray._do_check_updates` downloaded + scheduled the installer correctly but then called `_do_quit()`, which schedules `tk_root.after(0, quit)` - and that SILENTLY FAILS because the menu callback runs on the pystray WORKER thread (Python 3.13/3.14 reject Tcl calls, incl. after(), off the main thread). So the tray never quit, held the exe file locks, and the scheduled installer reverted → the manual update "didn't go through" (Tiago). The AUTO-update path (`_check_updates_silent`) worked because it runs where after() succeeds.

def _shop_dismiss_if_finished(adb: ADB, frame, pills: dict) -> bool:
    """Close the merchant panel once we're done buying. Returns True if we acted.

    Driven by "are we FINISHED with the shop", never by "does the shop still
    show stock" - a panel whose rows have all sold out shows zero green pills
    while remaining fully open on top of the Leave diamond.

    Two rungs, because the two known dismisses differ:
      1. KEYCODE_BACK - the game's own panel dismiss (validated live
         2026-08-16: one press closed it within 2s).
      2. A tap on empty screen well left of the panel - an outside-tap. This
         is the one the field report describes working by hand ("se eu clico
         no meio pra sair do mercador"), so it is the rung that matches what
         users have actually confirmed. Worst case with no panel up it is a
         map tap; SHADOW-EXIT re-teleports the hero within ~7s, so it cannot
         strand anyone.
    """
    opened_at = _shop_visit["opened_at"]
    finished = (_shop_visit["done"]
                or _shop_visit["taps"] >= _SHOP_MAX_TAPS
                or (opened_at
                    and time.monotonic() - opened_at > _SHOP_STUCK_S))
    if not (_shop_visit["opened"] and finished):
        return False
    if _shop_visit["closes"] >= _SHOP_MAX_CLOSES:
        return False
    now = time.monotonic()
    if now - _shop_visit["last_close_at"] < 2.5:
        return False
    _shop_visit["closes"] += 1
    _shop_visit["last_close_at"] = now
    n = _shop_visit["closes"]

        adb.keyevent("KEYCODE_BACK")
        log.info("portal merchant: finished, panel may still be up - BACK to "
                 "close it (%d/%d, pills=%d)", n, _SHOP_MAX_CLOSES, len(pills))

                 "@ %d,%d (%d/%d, pills=%d)", x, y, n, _SHOP_MAX_CLOSES,
                 len(pills))
    return True

ship 0.5.99 — close the merchant panel that was still trapping people

Field report (pt-BR, 2026-08-16): "Ele fica aberto do mercador. Se eu clico
no meio pra sair do mercador, ele vai no portal e teleporta." The bot buys,
the shop panel stays open on top of the Leave diamond, and manually tapping
the middle of the screen to dismiss it lets the bot walk out immediately.

0.5.98 already had a BACK rung for exactly this and it did not fire, because
it sat BELOW `if len(pills) < 3: return False`. A shop whose remaining rows
have all sold out shows zero green pills, so a fully-open panel reads as
len(pills)==0, logs the flatly untrue "panel closed", and returns early. The
0.5.98 validation passed only because that particular shop still happened to
show three Buy pills — the fix was right, its position in the function was
not.

Reworked as _shop_dismiss_if_finished(), called BEFORE the pill gate and
driven by "have we finished shopping", never by "does the shop still have
stock":
  - rung 1 KEYCODE_BACK (validated live 2026-08-16, closed it in one press)
  - rung 2 outside-tap mid-screen — the dismiss users confirmed by hand
  - armed from the Merchant TAP, not from later seeing >=3 pills, so a shop
    that opens already sold out is still dismissable
  - 45s backstop for a shop that never shows a buyable row at all
  - capped 3/room, throttled 2.5s (the 0.5.5 unbounded-BACK lesson)

Also: the CC freeze ladder had exactly ONE rung — 60s of zero damage went
straight to forceStuckExit and threw the chest away. Live test on 0.5.98
reached round 4/5 twice and forfeited both times, identically at 20x and at
<=5x, so it is not speed desync. Inside a CC, BOTH freeze mitigations were
disabled by `if not ccFzIdx`: the RE-ENGAGE sweep and the speed drop. And
CC-FREEZE-FIX cleared Monster.noCheckBattle without ever re-running
checkBattle — it opened the gate and nothing walked through, which is why it
logged 10 times while the round stayed frozen. Now tiered, mirroring what
non-CC akasa freezes already get:
  1. re-engage sweep at 10s flat (idempotent, moves no hero, cannot fight
     the CC's anchor pin)
  2. InfoDungeon.recover() x2 — proven safe in-CC by the CC-DEATH-RETRY path
     ("recover SUCCEEDED -> dungeon restored [CC re-detect]"). recover, NOT
     retry: retry re-enters the scene and would drop the round progress.
  3. forfeit, as before.

Relay: SPEED-DESYNC-DROP is emitted by the lua but was in NEITHER pattern in
game_state.py, so it could never reach bot.log — we were blind fleet-wide to
whether the mitigation ever fired. Added, with the new CC-RE-ENGAGE. Both
verified to actually match the regex rather than assumed.
[[feedback_marker_must_reach_botlog]]

NOT yet validated live: no portal room or CC hit has occurred since deploying
(the portal needs Akasa floor 338+ and the CC lottery hits ~4%). Shipped on
the user's call because people are stuck right now and the risk is bounded —
worst case for the outside-tap is a map tap that SHADOW-EXIT undoes within
~7s, and worst case for the CC rungs is the same forfeit that happens today.

    # Live 2026-08-16 shadow_challenge_10: BACK closed the panel cleanly at

    # stray map taps. The dismiss cannot see the panel disappear (it returns
    # True and short-circuits the tick before the panel-closed check runs), so
    # gate the escalation on evidence instead: no pills means nothing left to
    # dismiss. Rung 1 (BACK) still fires unconditionally, since a fully
    # sold-out panel is invisible to the pill detector.
    if _shop_visit["closes"] >= 1 and not pills:
        return False
    now = time.monotonic()

def _cc_canon_note_fin(button: str, fin: int | None) -> None:
    """Record a canonical tap of `button` taken while fin was `fin`.

    A changed fin means the previous taps worked - clear the counter. An
    unchanged fin means that tap achieved nothing; count it.
    """

        _cc_canon_fin[button] = fin

def _cc_canonical(button: str, fallback: tuple[int, int]) -> tuple[int, int]:
    """v0.3.92: snap a CC button tap to the canonical pixel for the
    current resolution, falling back to the matcher's center if we
    don't have ground truth for this resolution.

    Caller passes the matched-pixel center as `fallback` so resolutions
    we haven't catalogued keep their existing behavior - this can't
    regress users on 1280x720 / 1920x1080 / 960x540 / etc."""
    canon = _CC_CANONICAL.get((SCREEN_W, SCREEN_H))
    if canon is None:
        return fallback
    target = canon.get(button, fallback)
    if target == fallback:
        return target
    # v0.5.89: canonical is the DEFAULT, not the last word. It exists to beat
    # decoy scatter (0.3.92) and is right on the resolutions it was derived
    # from - but a stale entry is unfalsifiable: we keep tapping a dead pixel
    # forever while the matcher points somewhere else. Field log 662log.txt
    # 2026-08-13 (1600x900): Open Chest tapped at the canonical (1507,581) 12
    # times while 12 of 14 matches agreed on (1473,519) - 62 px away, score
    # 0.93. fin sat at 5 (rounds won, chest unopened) for 105s and 231s on the
    # two CCs that eventually opened, and a third was still stuck at 223s when
    # the owner intervened.
    #
    # So: give the canonical the first _CC_CANON_GRACE taps at a given fin. If
    # fin STILL hasn't advanced after that, the canonical is not working here -
    # defer to the matcher. Costs nothing where the canonical is correct (fin
    # advances on the first tap or two and the counter resets), and self-heals
    # the stale-entry case without anyone guessing a new pixel.
    stuck = _cc_canon_miss.get(button, 0)
    if stuck >= _CC_CANON_GRACE and fallback != (0, 0):
        log.warning("CC canonical %s @ %s hasn't advanced fin in %d taps - "
                    "deferring to matched %s", button, target, stuck, fallback)
        return fallback
    return target

currency to spend on it."

With no funds the Buy pill stays lit, so the bot taps it and the game answers
with an "insufficient" popup — which HIDES the Buy pills. pills==0 then looks
identical to "the panel closed", and 0.5.101's guard
(`if closes >= 1 and not pills: return False`) suppressed every escalation
past the first BACK. My own regression: that guard was added in 0.5.101 to
stop the stray map taps from 0.5.100, and "pills gone because it closed" vs
"pills gone because a popup covers them" are the same observation, so
suppressing on it re-broke the second case.

The signal that actually separates them is a matched portal diamond: if
Leave/Merchant is visible, the panel is provably gone. So:

    disarming the dismiss for real rather than by guessing from pill count
  - the no-pills case is throttled (12s) instead of blocked, so a covering
    popup still gets BACK then outside-taps

    backstop could spend all 3 attempts while we were still trying to buy,
    leaving nothing to clear the panel with once we finally gave up.

(MAX_TAPS=5, MAX_CLOSES=3, STUCK_S=45): 5 futile Buy taps -> done -> fresh

def _proactive_refresh_due(runs_since_refresh: int, every_n: int,
                           elapsed_s: float = 0.0, every_s: float = 0.0) -> bool:
    """v0.5.78 / v0.5.81: whether a proactive game refresh is due - by run count
    OR by elapsed time since the last game (re)start, whichever comes first.

    Each axis disables independently (every_n<=0 / every_s<=0 = off). The TIME
    axis is what makes this fire in CC-RUSH mode: there the lottery rerolls barely
    tick runs_completed (field: 63 dungeon-exits but only 3 completed runs in
    35 min), so the run axis alone would take hours and never recycle the game
    before it wedges. The CALLER only invokes this at the safe between-runs point
    (at camp, not paused, not mid crash-recovery)."""
    by_runs = every_n > 0 and runs_since_refresh >= every_n
    by_time = every_s > 0 and elapsed_s >= every_s
    return by_runs or by_time

back — confirming the run axis is off and the time axis drives it.

# --- CC RUSH pipeline triage -------------------------------------------------
# The CC flow is strictly sequential: scan -> hit -> arm -> route -> open round
# -> press -> fin advances -> chest claimed. It can only break at ONE of those,
# and the FIRST stage reading zero is the one that broke. Support spent
# 2026-08-16/17 diffing logs by hand to find that stage on reports of "same
# version, works for them and not for me"; putting it in the bundle means the
# answer arrives WITH the report instead of after a round trip.
_TRIAGE_STAGES = [
    ("1 lottery scans",   r"cc detect: "),
    ("2 lottery HIT",     r"cc detect: .*HIT"),
    ("3 armed",           r"CC FULL AUTO armed|cc auto watch"),
    ("4 routed/teleport", r"cc auto teleport"),
    ("5 round fired",     r"cc auto round"),
    ("6 button pressed",  r"CC FULL AUTO: (?:long-pressed|PRESS-BEGIN)"),
    ("7 fin advanced",    r"STEP-DIAG fin=[1-9]"),
    ("8 chest claimed",   r"CC-AUTO-SOLVED|Open Chest"),
]
_TRIAGE_ENV = [
    ("bot/lua version", r"LUA-VERSION.*|LUA-SKEW.*"),
    ("display size",    r"display size: \d+x\d+"),
    ("emulator inst",   r"instance=\S+"),
    ("watchdogs",       r"restart watchdogs:.*"),
]
_TRIAGE_FAIL = [
    ("freeze exits",   r"CC-FREEZE-EXIT"),
    ("freeze recover", r"CC-FREEZE-RECOVER"),
    ("bailed",         r"CC-AUTO-BAILED"),
    ("band rejects",   r"outside expected .*band"),
    ("deaths",         r"battle-lose popup opened"),
    ("game crashes",   r"game crash marker"),
    ("paused+dead",    r"PAUSED-AND-DEAD"),
    ("bot suspended",  r"active actions suspended"),
]


def triage_text(log_data) -> str:
    """One-page 'which stage broke' summary of a bot.log."""
    if isinstance(log_data, bytes):
        txt = log_data.decode("utf-8", "replace")
    else:
        txt = log_data or ""
    out = ["CC RUSH pipeline triage",
           "(each stage feeds the next; the FIRST zero is where it broke)", ""]
    out.append("-- environment --")
    for label, pat in _TRIAGE_ENV:
        m = re.search(pat, txt)
        out.append("  %-16s %s" % (label, m.group(0) if m else "-- ABSENT --"))
    out.append("")
    out.append("-- toggles seen --")
    for label, pat in (("rush", r"cc ui: rush \w+"),
                       ("pause", r"overlay pause -> \w+")):
        hits = re.findall(pat, txt)
        out.append("  %-16s %s" % (label, hits[:8] if hits else "-- none --"))
    out.append("")
    out.append("-- pipeline --")
    for label, pat in _TRIAGE_STAGES:
        n = len(re.findall(pat, txt))
        out.append("  %-18s %6d  %s" % (label, n, "#" * min(30, n)))
    out.append("")
    out.append("-- failure markers --")
    for label, pat in _TRIAGE_FAIL:
        out.append("  %-16s %6d" % (label, len(re.findall(pat, txt))))
    return chr(10).join(out) + chr(10)

working machine against a broken one becomes reading one row.

which is the entire diagnosis, visible without reading a log line.

support code" tray item; the bundle already carried bot.log, adb, bluestacks,
logcat and meminfo. This just answers the question the bundle was collected

def step_install_apk(*, allow_destructive_reinstall: bool = False) -> None:
    # Stop game first to avoid mid-install issues; don't fail if it isn't running.
    subprocess.run([ADB, "-s", _device(), "shell", "am", "force-stop", PACKAGE],
                   check=False, capture_output=True)
    # v0.5.77: make sure the device is actually ONLINE before installing, not
    # merely present. See _wait_for_device_online - the plain `adb connect`
    # here used to return while BlueStacks still reported the device 'offline',
    # and the install fired into that window failed instantly (the fleet code-4).
    _wait_for_device_online()

    splits = _read_splits()
    if splits:
        # App Bundle path: install-multiple expects every APK in the session.
        # All have been re-signed with our keystore in step_sign_apk.
        apks = [str(APK_OUTPUT)] + [str(_signed_split_path(Path(s))) for s in splits]
        install_cmd_prefix = [ADB, "-s", _device(), "install-multiple", "-r"]
        log.info("installing %d APKs via install-multiple (1 base + %d splits)",
                 len(apks), len(apks) - 1)
    else:
        # Single-APK path (older / non-bundle installs).
        apks = [str(APK_OUTPUT)]
        install_cmd_prefix = [ADB, "-s", _device(), "install", "-r"]

    # 60s per attempt. A 290MB APK over loopback adb-install on a healthy
    # BlueStacks finishes in 30-90s; if the first attempt blows the cap,
    # BlueStacks's PackageInstaller / adb server is wedged (cert-mismatch
    # deadlock against a previously-installed copy, or a BlueStacks-
    # internal lock that never releases). v0.2.76: instead of waiting
    # the historical 8 minutes and then dumping the user with a

    # blip they never notice. If recovery doesn't fix it (BlueStacks
    # itself wedged, not just adb), the second attempt raises the

def _proactive_refresh_due(runs_since_refresh: int, every_n: int,
                           elapsed_s: float = 0.0, every_s: float = 0.0) -> bool:
    """v0.5.78 / v0.5.81: whether a proactive game refresh is due - by run count
    OR by elapsed time since the last game (re)start, whichever comes first.

    Each axis disables independently (every_n<=0 / every_s<=0 = off). The TIME
    axis is what makes this fire in CC-RUSH mode: there the lottery rerolls barely
    tick runs_completed (field: 63 dungeon-exits but only 3 completed runs in
    35 min), so the run axis alone would take hours and never recycle the game
    before it wedges. The CALLER only invokes this at the safe between-runs point
    (at camp, not paused, not mid crash-recovery)."""
    by_runs = every_n > 0 and runs_since_refresh >= every_n
    by_time = every_s > 0 and elapsed_s >= every_s
    return by_runs or by_time

name: project_game_memory_leak_investigation
description: "LOCALIZED 2026-08-18: the fleet-wide game leak is the GAME's native scene memory, driven by CC RUSH lottery rerolls (~39MB/min), not our lua and not BlueStacks under-provisioning. Fixed by a measured PSS refresh axis in 0.5.110."

**LOCALIZED 2026-08-18 on the dev BlueStacks. It is the GAME's native scene memory, and CC RUSH is what drives it.** Paired measurement, one session, `dumpsys meminfo com.r2games.ah` sampled every 60s:

| phase | duration | PSS |
|---|---|---|
| ordinary akasa farming | 25 min | **FLAT 490-515 MB** |
| CC RUSH on | 12 min | **514 -> 981 MB (~39 MB/min)** |

The growth is **Native Heap (+228MB) + Private Other (+157MB); Java heap stays flat at 12-14MB and Graphics reads 0** (BlueStacks doesn't itemize GPU). That kills the "our lua tables" hypothesis outright — see below.

**MECHANISM: dungeon scene load/unload churn.** The CC lottery rerolls floor 1 looking for a Challenge Chest and exits immediately on a MISS — measured **~5 rerolls/min** (`dungeon_exit!` + `cc lottery: exit OK` + `run N/inf complete`, 16 of each in 3 min). Ordinary akasa farming enters a floor **0.19x/min — 26x less churn**. Each reroll is a full scene load+unload the game never fully frees. Restarting the game reclaims it all: 1,127,442K -> 344,748K, native 467,432K -> 35,844K, back in-scene in 48s, CC RUSH resumes 15s later with `longest=` streak state intact.

**THIS IS WHY CC RUSH "works for one user and not another" on the SAME version.** At 39 MB/min a CC-RUSH machine crosses the ~1.3GB tap-dropping level in about 20 minutes (field bundle 6FB5B654: 1,363,284K, Challenge button matched at 0.94 and tapped on the correct pixel 12x in 2 min with the game ignoring every one). An akasa-only machine never gets there. **CC RUSH is self-poisoning: the more it rerolls, the sooner the game stops registering the tap that opens the chest.** The discriminator was never resolution or a bad install — it is game-process uptime *in CC RUSH mode*.

**OUR LUA IS NOT THE LEAK — proven, don't relitigate.** The LUA-MEM probe (bot_autopilot.lua, logs `collectgarbage("count")` every 60s) shows the Lua VM heap **sawtoothing normally with a stable floor**: 252MB->204MB, 296MB->181MB. A first 10-minute sample (194->304MB, peak==heap every sample) looked like an unbounded lua leak and I nearly shipped a 5-minute forced-GC on the strength of it — **that was one growth phase of a normal sawtooth, and PSS was FLAT across the whole window anyway.** Sample long enough to see a collection before calling something a leak. `runMemoryCleanup()` was left at its 25-min cadence and camp-only gate on purpose; the only real bug there was `os.clock()` (CPU-time, ~0.55x wallclock -> a "25 min" gate really waited ~45) fixed to `os.time()`.

**THE FIX (0.5.110): a MEASURED refresh axis.** `game_pss_kb()` in game_state.py parses the App Summary `TOTAL:` line (colon form — `dumpsys` prints two totals and the table row's columns shift). bot.py samples it at the existing between-runs refresh gate, cached `FARMER_PSS_SAMPLE_S` (120s), and `_proactive_refresh_due()` gained a third axis: restart at `FARMER_REFRESH_PSS_MB` (default **1100**, ~250MB under the confirmed wedge and ~2x a healthy plateau). Run-count and elapsed-time are both *proxies* for leak size and they are **wrong by 26x between modes** — a 180-min timer cannot fire before a CC-RUSH game wedges, and a 20-min timer would restart an akasa farm ~50x/day for nothing. The measured axis is self-targeting: akasa machines never trip it, CC RUSH recycles every ~15 min (48s cost, ~5% overhead). Validated end-to-end live: `1106 MB -> refresh -> 503 MB`.

**Older framing that still holds:** never answer "game keeps closing / OOM" with "add RAM" — a 2D cocos2d-x game at 1.4GB is a leak. `collect-logcat.bat` captures the meminfo breakdown (device auto-detect + timestamped). Ruled out earlier and still ruled out: wrapper-stacking, RPC-sniffer accumulation.

Related: [[project_proactive_game_refresh]] (the refresh mechanism this hooks into), [[project_cc_stale_canonical_tap]] (the tap-drop symptom), [[project_reengage_dead_49_versions]] (same lesson: don't ship an unmeasured "improvement"), [[feedback_lua_clock_semantics]], [[project_adb_version_war_ldplayer]], [[project_vm_restart_kill_no_relaunch]].

name: feedback_ship_from_head_snapshot
description: "When isolating a fix from in-tree WIP, build the lua bundle from a git-HEAD snapshot (not the working tree) and verify the uploaded R2 object by re-downloading"

When shipping an isolated fix while unrelated WIP sits uncommitted in the same files, **do NOT build the lua bundle from the working tree** - `tools/build_lua_bundle.py` reads `patches/*.lua` live, and if an editor (VS Code) has the WIP file open it can AUTOSAVE the WIP back over your clean disk write between the dry-run and the upload. This happened 2026-06-20 shipping 0.5.28: a clean dry-run (249KB, no Bazaar) was followed seconds later by an upload that re-included ~480 lines of Bazaar WIP, because the editor re-saved `bot_autopilot.lua` (mtime jumped, size = the WIP backup size).

**Why:** the working tree is a shared, externally-mutated surface during an active session; a clean read at T0 does not guarantee clean bytes at T1.

**How to apply:**
1. Extract each bundle file with `git show HEAD:patches/<f>` into a private dir the editor isn't watching (e.g. `_ship_clean/`), apply the fix there, build the zip from THAT dir, upload.
2. ALWAYS verify the uploaded artifact by re-downloading it: `wrangler r2 object get abyss-bot-downloads/lua/<v>.zip --remote --file check.zip`, then unzip and grep for both the fix marker AND the WIP marker (expect fix=present, WIP=absent). Don't trust the local build - verify the REMOTE bytes.
3. For the commit, place the clean file + `git add` + `git commit` in ONE chained command to minimize the autosave race window, then confirm with `git show HEAD:patches/<f> | grep -c <wip-marker>` == 0.

Also: `winget install JRSoftware.InnoSetup` installs ISCC per-user at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Inno Setup 6\ISCC.exe` (NOT Program Files) - `farmer.iss` hardcodes the Program Files path in a comment but the binary works from the LocalAppData path. Full release flow + R2 auth in [[reference_release_flow]].

Every version bump in `version.py` requires a matching `lua/<version>.zip` upload to the `abyss-bot-downloads` R2 bucket - even when no lua patches changed. The worker's `/v1/lua` endpoint keys by version (`(LUA_PREFIX || "lua/") + version + ".zip"` in worker.js luaBundle), so a missing object returns 404 → `license_client` raises `LicenseError` → `bot.py --patch-only` exits 3 → tray shows "Patching failed (code 3)". Run: `python tools\build_lua_bundle.py` (reads VERSION from version.py and uploads via wrangler).

**Why:** Caused the 0.3.19 code-3 incident on 2026-05-12. I shipped bot.py-only changes for the orb-variant Challenge button position fix, bumped to 0.3.19, built+uploaded the new installer .exe and manifest.json, but forgot the lua bundle because "no lua changed." Every customer auto-updating got the 404.

**How to apply:** Ship checklist for any version bump - (1) update version.py + farmer.iss, (2) PyInstaller tray + bot, (3) ISCC installer, (4) sha256 the .exe, (5) update manifest.json, (6) `wrangler r2 object put abyss-bot-downloads/abyss-bot-setup-<v>.exe` + `manifest.json`, (7) **`python tools\build_lua_bundle.py`** (uploads lua/<v>.zip), (8) commit. Step 7 is mandatory regardless of whether patches/*.lua changed.

reclaims all of it (1,127,442K -> 344,748K, back in-scene in 48s).

This is why CC RUSH "works for one user and not another" on the SAME
version: at 39 MB/min a CC-RUSH machine crosses the ~1.3GB tap-dropping
level in ~20 min (bundle 6FB5B654: button matched 0.94, correct pixel
tapped 12x, game ignored every one). It self-poisons. Never was
resolution or a bad install.

The fix is a MEASURED refresh axis. Run count and elapsed time are both
proxies for leak size and they are wrong by 26x between modes — a
180-min timer cannot fire before a CC-RUSH game wedges, and a 20-min
timer would restart an akasa farm ~50x/day for nothing.

  game_state.py  game_pss_kb() parses the App Summary "TOTAL:" line
                 (colon form: dumpsys prints two totals and the table
                 row's columns shift)
  bot.py         samples it at the existing between-runs gate, cached
                 FARMER_PSS_SAMPLE_S (120s), and _proactive_refresh_due
                 gains a third axis at FARMER_REFRESH_PSS_MB (1100)

1100 MB sits ~250MB under the confirmed wedge and ~2x a healthy
plateau, so it is self-targeting: akasa never trips it, CC RUSH
recycles every ~15 min at 48s cost. Validated end to end live:
1106 MB -> refresh -> 503 MB, rush resumed with streak state intact.

Also: LUA-MEM probe (bot_autopilot) logs the Lua VM heap every 60s —
it is what rules our lua out next time, and it shows a normal sawtooth
with a stable floor (252->204, 296->181MB). A first 10-min sample
looked like an unbounded lua leak and nearly bought a forced GC every
5 min; that was one growth phase, and PSS was flat across it anyway.
runMemoryCleanup keeps its 25-min cadence and camp-only gate; the only
real bug there was os.clock() (CPU-time, ~0.55x wallclock, so "25 min"
really waited ~45) -> os.time().

CC-UNREACH-DIAG (bot_akasa_nav) logs the inputs of the 90s unreachable
bail, which bundle 1B043DE8 shows not firing with every visible
condition satisfied. All three markers added to the game_state relay
whitelist — without that they can never reach bot.log.

def _shop_buy_pills(frame) -> dict[int, tuple[int, int]]:
    """Map row index -> tap point for every visible green Buy pill.

    Absent rows are sold out (or off-panel). Row index is derived from the
    pill's absolute y, so row 1 selling out never promotes row 2 into its
    slot.
    """
    fh, fw = frame.shape[:2]
    x0, x1 = int(fw * _SHOP_BUY_X_FRAC[0]), int(fw * _SHOP_BUY_X_FRAC[1])
    row0_y = fh * _SHOP_ROW0_Y_FRAC
    pitch = fh * _SHOP_ROW_PITCH_FRAC
    min_area = _SHOP_MIN_PILL_AREA_720P * (fw / 1280.0) * (fh / 720.0)
    hsv = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2HSV)
    mask = cv2.inRange(hsv, (25, 60, 80), (45, 255, 255))
    mask[:, :x0] = 0
    mask[:, x1:] = 0
    count, _, stats, _ = cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats(mask)
    pills: dict[int, tuple[int, int]] = {}
    for i in range(1, count):
        x, y, w, h, area = stats[i]
        if area < min_area:
            continue
        row = round((y - row0_y) / pitch)
        # Reject anything that isn't sitting on the row grid - a partially
        # scrolled row or an unrelated green element would otherwise get a
        # bogus row index and could be tapped as if it were row 1.
        if abs(y - (row0_y + row * pitch)) > 12 * (fh / 720.0):
            continue
        if row >= 0:
            pills[row] = (int(x + w // 2), int(y + h // 2))
    return pills

New red portal on the akasa map (first reported 2026-08-13). Nav already enters it and clears the boss + loot on its own; 0.5.86 added the two missing steps - buy the top two shop rows, and leave properly instead of sitting in the room.

**The portal room's UI slot is a trap.** `Enter`, `Merchant`, `Leave` (and the akasa `Return`, and every CC button) all render as the SAME cream rhombus at (1080,483) on 720p. The shape carries zero information - this is the decoy family that sent 0.3.93-0.2.95 chasing the wrong half of the screen. So `bt_portal_leave.png` / `bt_portal_merchant.png` are **text-only crops of the label**, not the diamond: 1.00 on their own frame, 0.49 on the other's. Matched inside `_cc_btn_roi()`, threshold 0.80, scales locked to 1.0 in the roi.json (rescaling blurs the glyph differences that ARE the signal).

**The shop is keyed by geometry, not templates.** Every row's green Buy pill is identical and evenly pitched (x=1151 w=91 h=62; rows y=58/193/328/464/599, pitch 135.4), so no template can distinguish row 1 from row 4. `_shop_buy_pills()` colour-keys the pills (HSV 25-45 hue) and indexes by ABSOLUTE y against that grid - so row 1 selling out can never promote row 2 into its slot, and the randomised stock can't break it. A bought row loses its pill entirely, which doubles as the done-signal. Capped at 5 taps/visit because a misfire spends premium currency. Only rows 1-2 (the "Ancient ..." pair, red-gem currency) are bought; rows 3+ are consumables, deliberately skipped for the same reason as `isPotionMerchant()` in the lua.

**Two gotchas worth keeping:**
- `Leave` is NOT gated on having shopped first. A portal whose merchant we never reach would otherwise trap the bot in the room forever - worse than missing two buys.
- The Leave diamond stays visible BEHIND the confirm modal, and that modal spans only x365-915. Re-tapping the diamond at x=1080 lands OUTSIDE it, dismisses it, and drops the follow-up Confirm onto the map (walks the hero). Guarded by a 20s window scoped to our own Leave tap so it can't grab the retry / back-to-camp modals other flows own.
- The confirm modal needed NO new template: `bt_confirm_modal.png` scores 1.00 on it at the existing canonical (757,460), so `_tap_restart_confirm()` is reused as-is.

**Reproduced LIVE on the dev box 2026-08-18 (0.5.109), and it is the answer to "why isn't it solving the CC on my own machine".** 112 consecutive BLIND Challenge long-presses over 13 minutes, every one logging `attempt=0/5`, while the CC lottery forfeited and left the dungeon every ~10s underneath:

    CC FULL AUTO: BLIND Challenge long-press @ 1046,486 (4000ms) — no frame
    match in 809s of arrived+fin=0 (reach=false anchor churn). attempt=0/5

**THE PROOF TECHNIQUE: `_cc_auto_stuck_tick` sets `stuck_count = 1` on its FIRST call, so a reported 0 after 112 presses proves the function was NEVER CALLED.** A counter that reads 0 is categorically different from one that reads 1 — use that to distinguish "not incrementing" from "not invoked".

**Root cause, one line** (`bot.py`, blind-press path): `if arrived and _cc_auto_stuck_tick("challenge", 0):`. The enclosing block is entered on `(arrived or round_fired)`. On a **reach=false** anchor, `round_fired` (openChance fires at DETECTION) unblocks the press while the hero never arrives, so `arrived` stays False, the tick never runs, and the press is unbounded.

**ONE frozen variable disabled TWO mechanisms, which is why it read as two unrelated bugs:** the indoor/mine slot alternation keys off `stuck_count % 2`, so a permanently-0 counter always took the even branch. The dev box is 1280x720, where `_CC_CANONICAL` knows the Challenge button is at **(1086,485)** — and it tapped **(1046,486) 112 times without ever trying it**. When a counter both BOUNDS a retry and SELECTS what to retry, freezing it looks like "gives up never" plus "never finds the button".

**Fix 0.5.112: count every blind press under a DISTINCT key with its own budget.**
- `_cc_auto_stuck_tick("challenge_blind", 0, _CC_BLIND_STUCK_LIMIT)` — a separate button key keeps this OFF the match-press budget, so **0.5.49's arrived-gating on the match-press stays untouched. Do not "simplify" that away**: it is measured (214 fin=0 deaths against 1208 reach=false anchors) and exists because pre-arrival match-presses were killing CCs on slow-arrival maps.
- `_CC_BLIND_STUCK_LIMIT = 20`, NOT the shared 5. Blind presses begin only `_CC_FIN0_BLIND_AFTER_S` = **12s** after arming, so a limit of 5 gives up ~60s in and re-creates the exact 0.5.49 regression. 20 at the ~10s cadence lands near 200s, just under the lua's **240s AUTO_STALL_S**, so bot.py stops burning taps right before the watchdog that owns the exit takes over.
- Verified: bails on press 20 having tried BOTH slots (canonical 10x, variant 9x, canonical FIRST as the dominant 173/200 historical position). Match-press re-checked, still bails at exactly 5.

**STILL OPEN — the stale arm itself.** `cc_auto_active` is cleared ONLY by a lua `CC-AUTO-DONE`; nothing else, notably NOT `dungeon_exit`. So an armed-but-unreachable CC survives the lottery forfeiting and leaving, and bot.py keeps running CC logic on lottery reroll maps (`#fc_abyss1`, `#lava_abyss1`) that never had a CC. Proof it survives: `armed_age` climbs monotonically 741→840s straight through `cc lottery: exit OK` firing every ~10s. **DO NOT fix this by clearing on `dungeon_exit`** — 0.3.115 did exactly that, users reported CC RUSH got worse fleet-wide, and 0.3.116 reverted it (see the comment at `game_state.py:1160`). It needs a signal that cannot fire during a healthy CC; the `cc lottery: MISS ... forfeiting` marker is a candidate, since a floor with no CC cannot have a valid armed one.

straight back off, and it teleported again -- 49 times over ~9 minutes before
anything gave up. That is the "keeps teleporting to the CC and then walks away
from it" report, exactly.

The CC-UNREACH-DIAG shipped in 0.5.110 answered it on the first occurrence:

    idx=4 fin=0 cheb=1 best=0 since=... elapsed=465s bail_at=90s
    anchor=14,38 branch=blocked          (18 samples, all identical)

elapsed=465s against bail_at=90s. The bail could not arm because of best=0,
and best=0 is OUR OWN DOING: the anchor centre 14,38 is unwalkable, so
CC-AUTO-TELEPORT-SHIFT relocates the destination to the walkable 13,37 beside
it, which records best=0 on the first tick. CC_UNREACH_BAIL_S is gated on
`best > 1` -- deliberately, and the 0.5.64 comment says why: a CC the hero got
onto is not "unreachable", and a non-advancing fight there "is a different
problem and must not be thrown away here". Correct reasoning. The problem is
that the different problem had no handler.

With the fast wallclock bail structurally blocked, the only backstop left was
AUTO_STALL_S = 240 measured in nowR = os.clock = CPU-TIME. Measured here at
0.51x wallclock (armedFor 10s -> 236s across 446 real seconds), so the true
give-up was ~470s. Hence nine minutes.

Fix: a third branch for the adjacent-but-not-advancing case, on os.time()
wallclock like CC_UNREACH_BAIL_S.

    elseif best <= 1 then   -> CC_ADJ_STALL_BAIL_S = 180

180s is well past bot.py's own press budget (it had already bailed 5 matched

**THE DIAGNOSTIC PAID FOR ITSELF.** `CC-UNREACH-DIAG` (shipped 0.5.110 for precisely this open question) answered it on the first occurrence, 18 identical samples:

    idx=4 fin=0 cheb=1 best=0 since=... elapsed=465s bail_at=90s anchor=14,38 branch=blocked

**THE TRAP: our own teleport disables our own bail.** The anchor centre 14,38 is unwalkable, so `CC-AUTO-TELEPORT-SHIFT` relocates the destination to the walkable **13,37** beside it. That records **best=0 on the very first tick**. `CC_UNREACH_BAIL_S` (90s, wallclock) is gated on **`best > 1`**, so it is disabled *forever* on any CC whose anchor needed a shift. The gate itself is CORRECT and documented (0.5.64): "a CC the hero got onto is not unreachable; a non-advancing fight there is a different problem and must not be thrown away here." **The bug was that the different problem had no handler at all.**

**Fallback was CPU-time, so ~2x too slow.** With the fast bail blocked, the only backstop was `AUTO_STALL_S = 240` measured in `nowR` = `now()` = **`os.clock()` = CPU-time**. Measured here at **0.51x wallclock** (`armedFor` grew 10s→236s across 446 real seconds — read the CC-AUTO-WATCH line's armedFor against log timestamps to get this ratio for free). True give-up ≈ 470s. See [[feedback_lua_clock_semantics]].

**FIX 0.5.113** — a third branch in the same if/elseif chain, on `os.time()`:

    elseif best <= 1 then   ->  CC_ADJ_STALL_BAIL_S = 180  ->  fireAutoExit("adjacent_stall_...")

180s clears bot.py's own press budget (5 matched presses, bailed at ~30s) and ~3 of the lua's 62s `reason=retry` cycles (7 changed nothing). Only reachable at `curFin == 0`, so a healthy fight cannot trip it — the instant a round lands, fin advances and the block is skipped. description: "CC never initiates = unreachable-anchor CCs (bbox fully unwalkable → hero stuck dist>=3 → gladiator round can't start even though openChance fires + Challenge press lands). massif detection was a false alarm."

Live-debugged on Tiago's box 2026-06-30/07-01 (0.5.52), incl. a 7h overnight
logcat capture. Conclusions CORRECTED by the overnight data:

**CORRECTION - "massif detection-dead" was WRONG (small-sample variance).** The
first session showed #massif 0 HITs / 222 scans while other maps hit - I called it
a de-facto blacklist. The overnight run: #massif **2 HITs** / 247, in line with
every other map (pl3 6, mine2 4, lava 3, fc 3, rn 2, dungeon 1 - CCs are just
rare). `isChallengeChest` is map-agnostic; no map is blacklisted; detection works
everywhere. The bbox/type diag I added to bot_akasa_nav.lua for this is
unnecessary - can be reverted.

**THE REAL BUG (confirmed, map-independent): unreachable-anchor CCs.** When a CC's
anchor tile AND its whole bbox are unwalkable, the gladiator round can't start.
Overnight proof, #lava idx=9: `CC-DETECT HIT wh=4,4` → `CC-AUTO-TELEPORT-RING
center=19,13 bbox-full unwalkable -> walkable=13,11 cheb=6` (ring search lands the
hero 6 tiles away) → hero walks to dist=3, `CC-REACH-DIAG reach=false
blacklisted=true` → `CC-AUTO-ROUND openChance=true npcType=11` fired TWICE (new-cc
+ retry) → bot.py (alive) long-pressed Challenge repeatedly, **matched 0.93-0.96
AND blind-pressed**, for 163s → `curFin` never left 0. So openChance is NOT
position-independent (my earlier claim was wrong): the round needs the hero ON/
adjacent to the anchor, and neither the vision press nor openChance can start a
round the hero can't be positioned for. The churn (per-tick re-teleport to the ring
tile) is a symptom, not the cause. Reachable-anchor CCs work fully - idx=123
completed `fin 1→2→3→4→5→10` (claimed). Overnight: 96 openChance fires, several
completions, 4 freezes + 4 deaths.

**FIX DIRECTION (targeted, testable, NOT yet done):** for a fin=0 CC with
reach=false, draw the hero DIRECTLY onto the anchor center (e.g. 19,13) for
round-start instead of the ring-search walkable tile 6 away - the arena handles
combat positioning, so nav's "unwalkable" flag shouldn't gate the gladiator round.

**THE fix for "finds the chest but never initiates" / "teleports to the CC then walks away". Shipped 0.5.114, validated live twice.** The fix direction was written down 2026-06-30 in [[project_cc_massif_and_reachfalse_npcnil]] as "NOT yet done" and sat unimplemented for seven weeks while 0.5.112 and 0.5.113 only made the failure give up faster.

**ROOT CAUSE:** an unreachable-anchor CC has an unwalkable gladiator tile, so `CC-AUTO-TELEPORT-SHIFT` relocated the hero to the nearest walkable tile beside it. `NAV_gladiator.checkNearNpc` requires the hero **ON** the npc, so every Challenge press was refused — bot.py matched the button at **0.97** and long-pressed the exact matched pixel 5 times with `curFin` never leaving 0. **We were teleporting to the wrong tile on purpose.**

**THE BELIEF THAT WAS WRONG:** the 0.5.33 note says drawing onto the unwalkable centre "doesn't land the hero (engine clamps it off)". Not true for this call, and the codebase already contained two disproofs:
- the cache comment ~20 lines above the shift: *"a transient unit-block is fine, **draw() places the hero there anyway**"*
- **SHADOW-EXIT has done exactly this in production since 0.5.97** — draws onto the exit npc's own tile with `tgtWalk=false`, `post=` lands on target every time.
Both call the identical `pcall(global.player.draw, global.player, wx, wy, true)`. **When two paths use the same primitive and one demonstrably works, the difference is the ARGUMENT, not the mechanism.**

**FIX:** at `curFin == 0`, keep the anchor centre as the draw destination instead of shifting to a walkable neighbour (`CC-AUTO-ONCENTER` marker, whitelisted in game_state.py). **Scoped to fin==0 ONLY** — the shift still owns loot and fin>0 positioning, so every CC that works today is untouched and the only ones affected are those that never start at all. That scoping is what makes it safe to ship on one night's evidence.

**VALIDATED LIVE, worst case, twice.** Both with `shiftWouldBe=none` (the ENTIRE bbox unwalkable — previously the ring search, which strands the hero tiles away) and `reach=false len=-1` throughout:
- dev run idx=36: `CC-AUTO-ONCENTER` → `PLUG-CHANGE ... hero=47,13` (hero standing ON the unwalkable anchor) → `tapped Open Chest (fin=5/5, score=0.94)` → `fin 5 -> 10` → `CC FULL AUTO SOLVED`. **0→claimed in ~2.5 min.**
- user's machine idx=67: `CC-AUTO-ONCENTER center=63,36` → **fin=1 twenty-five seconds after arming** → `fin 1 -> 2`.
A reachable-anchor CC completed 1→5 in the same run, so the normal path is intact.

**Do NOT go the direct-RPC route** — v0.2.89 `ChanceUtils.gladiatorBattle` HUNG the game (disconnects autopilotTick's Looper). Teleport + bot.py vision press is the working architecture.

Related: [[project_cc_massif_and_reachfalse_npcnil]] (where the fix was first identified), [[project_cc_adjacent_stall_teleport_blocks_bail]] (the 180s bail that bounds this failure when it still happens), [[project_akasa_red_portal]] (SHADOW-EXIT, the production proof that draw lands on unwalkable tiles), [[feedback_no_batch_unvalidated_nav_lua]].

def _start_mainloop_liveness_watchdog(get_last_tick, hang_s: float,
                                      check_every_s: float = 30.0,
                                      on_hang=None) -> None:
    """v0.5.82: force-restart bot.py if its MAIN LOOP hangs.

    The tray auto-restarts bot.py when it EXITS, but a HANG - alive but frozen,
    e.g. an adb screencap/shell blocking for hours on a wedged BlueStacks during
    cold-start recovery - slips past that: every in-loop watchdog is itself stuck
    inside the frozen loop, so nothing fires. bot(7) 2026-07-22: one crash at
    02:06 wedged the recovery and the farm sat DEAD for 8 HOURS until a full
    restart. This runs on its OWN daemon thread (never blocked by the main
    thread's adb calls): it reads the main loop's last-tick timestamp and, once
    the loop hasn't ticked in hang_s, force-exits (os._exit) so the tray respawns
    a fresh bot.py - which restarts the adb server and re-attaches. hang_s must
    sit safely ABOVE the longest legitimate single-iteration block (the ~300s
    proactive game refresh), hence the 600s default - a 10-min-silent main loop
    is always a real hang, never normal work. on_hang defaults to os._exit(1);
    injectable for tests."""
    if hang_s <= 0:
        return
    _exit = on_hang or (lambda: os._exit(1))

    def _loop():
        while True:
            time.sleep(check_every_s)
            try:
                stale = time.monotonic() - get_last_tick()
            except Exception:
                continue
            if _mainloop_hang_exceeded(stale, hang_s):
                log.error("MAINLOOP-HANG: main loop has not ticked in %.0fs "
                          "(> %.0fs) - force-restarting bot.py so the tray "
                          "respawns a fresh one (wedged adb / stuck recovery).",
                          stale, hang_s)
                _exit()
                return

    threading.Thread(target=_loop, name="mainloop-liveness", daemon=True).start()

-- leave. An unknown npc id sorts with the merchant (rank 0), so
                -- a room with a shop we have not catalogued still gets visited
                -- before we walk out.
                local function scRankS(ed)
                    if ed.tag == "enter" then return 2 end
                    local idS = tostring(ed.info or ""):match("id=(%d+)")
                    if idS == SC_EXIT_NPC_ID then return 1 end
                    return 0
                end
                table.sort(npcsS, function(a, b)
                    local ra, rb = scRankS(a), scRankS(b)
                    if ra ~= rb then return ra < rb end
                    return (a.index or 0) < (b.index or 0)
                end)
                -- Keep tag=enter as the LAST-resort slot. shadow_challenge_8's
                -- enter is mode=1 (下楼/descend) and renders no diamond even
                -- with the hero standing on it, but the field is documented as
                -- "0-行走 1-下楼", so a mode=0 (walk) room may well exit through

"It cannot leave the portal AND cannot interact with the merchant" is ONE bug,
not two: a single early return in in_dungeon_step.

Live deadlock, shadow_challenge_14, 2026-08-19. Boss died at 13:08:20 ("kill
tick, room hp=1", then "magnet: battle ended"), a new group spawned two seconds
later (group=17000101) and nothing ever killed it, so monsters_active latched
True. `if state.monsters_active: return` sits ABOVE every portal handler, so
the reward popup, the merchant and the Leave diamond were all unreachable.
bot.py logged exactly ONE line in that room in four minutes -- its heartbeat --
while the lua cycled SHADOW-EXIT slots forever, which from the outside looks
like "it keeps teleporting to an empty space" (slot 3/3 is tag=enter, the
arrival portal, which renders no diamond).

The two sides disagreed about whether the room was finished, and the lua is the
one that knows: SHADOW-EXIT only runs post-boss. bot.py's job there is to tap a
modal diamond the lua has already parked the hero on; a lingering monster group
is not a reason to refuse. If a fight really is live the diamond is not
rendered, so the handlers find nothing and fall through.

Fix: run the three portal handlers BEFORE the monsters_active gate, scoped to
_in_portal_room() only. Everywhere else that gate is untouched -- it is what
stops bot.py tapping over live combat.

(13:07:01 -> 13:13:24); with the fix the bot found the Leave diamond on its

was wrong with detection; bot.py was never allowed to look.

"getMerchantInfo -> nil (needs the RPC form)", so the merchant-skip cannot be
written yet -- the no-arg accessor was a guess off bytecode strings and it is

def _compute_lua_hash() -> str:
    """SHA-256 over the post-placeholder lua chunks that would be injected
    on the next rebuild. Used as part of the patcher's cache key so the
    "skip rebuild" path can't fire across a lua bundle change with the
    same bot.VERSION (e.g., a same-day re-ship that only touches lua).

    Field log 2026-05-12: bot v0.3.12 through v0.3.16 all hit "skip
    rebuild" on the cache key (r2_base_version, bot_version, keystore)
    because version.VERSION incremented in step with the bot.py
    artifacts but the cache key didn't notice that the lua chunks
    themselves had changed across those re-ships. The customer's
    installed APK was effectively pinned at the lua from the last
    actual inject (0.2.94, weeks earlier) while bot.py reported it
    was running 0.3.16. Net result: nothing in the lua side of any
    0.3.07+ release ever reached the device. Embarrassing.

    Hashes are over the chunks dict in sorted key order for
    determinism; bytes go straight in, no JSON wrapper.
    """
    chunks = _load_lua_chunks()
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    for name in sorted(chunks.keys()):
        h.update(name.encode("utf-8"))
        h.update(b"\x00")
        h.update(chunks[name])
        h.update(b"\x00")
    return h.hexdigest()

**ROOT CAUSE:** `game_state._read_loop` cleared `game_dead_at` on **ANY** parsed lua event (v0.3.29, "proof of life"). Two of those are emitted by **our own module while the lua VM initialises**, i.e. on the LOGIN screen before any scene exists: **`bot_pause`** ("overlay pause -> RESUMED") and **`retry_dbg`** (the FRAME_battle_lose / InfoDungeon.recover wraps). def check_game_installed() -> CheckResult:
    """Try every known package name. The game has shipped as both
    com.f5game.ah and com.r2games.ah depending on the region/era; whichever
    is actually installed wins, and we pass that name down to the bot via
    CheckResult.package so the bot looks for the right pid."""
    adb = _adb_path()
    if not Path(adb).exists():
        return CheckResult("Game installed", False, "adb binary missing")
    device = _device()

    # If FARMER_PACKAGE is explicitly set, only check that one. Otherwise
    # try the known list in order.
    explicit = os.environ.get("FARMER_PACKAGE")
    candidates = (explicit,) if explicit else KNOWN_PACKAGES

    # `pm path` retry budget. Right after a fresh `install -r` of the ~115 MB
    # APK (the tray's post-patch verification at tray.py step 3.5), BlueStacks'
    # package manager is busy scanning + dexopting the new package, and
    # `pm path` routinely blocks past a 10 s timeout even though the package
    # IS installed - surfacing the false "patcher exited successfully but
    # com.r2games.ah isn't showing up" error (field report 2026-06-11).
    # `pm path` of a genuinely-absent package returns EMPTY immediately (not a
    # timeout), so retrying on timeout only ever costs time when pm is wedged/
    # busy - never on the fresh-customer "not installed" path. Retry a few
    # times with a longer per-attempt timeout before declaring failure.
    PM_ATTEMPTS = 4
    PM_TIMEOUT = 15
    PM_RETRY_SLEEP = 2.0

    last_err: Optional[str] = None
    for pkg in candidates:
        out: Optional[str] = None
        for attempt in range(1, PM_ATTEMPTS + 1):
            try:
                proc = subprocess.run(
                    [adb, "-s", device, "shell", "pm", "path", pkg],
                    capture_output=True, timeout=PM_TIMEOUT,
                )
                out = proc.stdout.decode(errors="replace")
                break  # got a clean reply (may or may not contain package:)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:

screen behind the dialog. The check was wrong, not the install.

   absent/offline device prints "error: device '127.0.0.1:5555' not found" on
   STDERR and leaves stdout empty; the code only tested `"package:" in out`, so

   claimed Abyss Hunters was not installed on a machine that had been farming
   all session.

   unauthorized / still connecting / protocol fault, and that path says plainly
   it is a CONNECTION problem and that nothing should be reinstalled. This
   matters more since 0.5.118/0.5.122: an emulator that comes back under its
   emulator-NNNN name is exactly this case.

2. The genuine not-installed path gave the user nothing to act on. It could not
   distinguish (a) we asked the WRONG DEVICE — second instance, or the
   emulator-NNNN / 127.0.0.1:<port> split, (b) a REGIONAL PACKAGE VARIANT not
   in KNOWN_PACKAGES (which is why this function tries a list at all), or
   (c) really absent. Those need opposite actions, and a support-code round
   trip is a bad trade when one `pm list packages` answers it on the spot.

   It now names the device it asked, lists any Abyss-Hunters-like packages that
   ARE installed there (with "set FARMER_PACKAGE to it"), and if the game is
   found on ANOTHER running device says "FOUND IT: <pkg> IS installed on
   <other> — set FARMER_DEVICE=<other>".

Verified: helper 6/6 on the transport-error strings; with BlueStacks closed the
check now reports the connection problem instead of a missing game; with it
running the happy path is unchanged ("com.r2games.ah present", package
correctly passed through).

ship 0.5.126 — the announcement dismisser was switched off exactly where the announcement appears

"Why did the game just restart on its own?" It did not restart on its own — the
silent-stall watchdog force-stopped it after the bot sat frozen in front of a
camp announcement for nine minutes.

    15:30:15  cold-start: announcement dismissed via KEYCODE_BACK (1/5)
    15:30:44  map: None -> camp
    ...       bot.py issues NOTHING for 9 minutes, runs=0,
              HEARTBEAT event_age climbing 235s -> 535s
    15:40:56  silent-stall watchdog: no logcat events for 602s -> force-stop

The game shows the announcement TWICE: once on the splash, and again a beat
after tap-to-start lands you in camp -- which the 0.3.13x boot-popup-clear
comment states explicitly. But the splash-drive gate required
`not state.current_map`, i.e. boot screens only, with its own comment saying
"Net: splash-drive fires for boot screens, never at camp". So the only code
that dismisses announcements was disabled precisely when the second one
appears. The boot-popup-clear window was meant to cover that gap, but it is
time-boxed and had already exited ("quiet 54s").

Fix: allow the dismiss at camp too, on a longer quiet window
(_CAMP_POPUP_QUIET_S = 120s, FARMER_CAMP_POPUP_QUIET_S). Gated on SILENCE, not
on being at camp: a live camp emits events every few seconds (map changes,
autosell, heroat), so two minutes of nothing is a modal holding the game. Well
under the 600s silent-stall threshold, so we now get a cheap dismiss attempt
before the expensive force-stop.

Gate verified across six cases: boot 30s dismisses (unchanged), boot 10s too
soon, CAMP 130s now dismisses (was dead), CAMP 30s untouched, paused never,
mid-dungeon never.

On the user's "is the banner text a prop?" theory: the template IS the literal
word "Announcement" (a 280x46 text crop), so that instinct was right in
principle -- but measured against the real frame from this incident it scores
1.000, and the log shows it dismissing correctly on the splash. For THIS
failure the detector was fine and the gate was wrong. A banner with a
different TITLE would still evade it; that is a separate, still-open risk and
needs a frame from a banner that actually fails to match.

Also answered: the game is NOT leaking at camp. Measured 728 -> 739 MB across
six minutes idle, i.e. ~2 MB/min. ~730 MB is simply camp's working set; the
leak is farming/rerolling only.

"Not opening the final CC chest again." Bundle 9896166B (0.5.126): an S-tier CC
fought all the way to fin 5/5 and was then abandoned WITHOUT A SINGLE TAP.

    16:03:22  open_chest stability arm @ 1051,531
    16:03:25  UNSTABLE prev=(1051,531) now=(1164,382) deferring (1/4)
    16:03:29  UNSTABLE ... deferring (2/4)
    16:03:33  UNSTABLE ... deferring (3/4)
    16:03:36  bailed - 5 consecutive 'open_chest' taps at fin=5 with no
              state advance (game UI likely frozen)

There is not one "tapped Open Chest" line in the entire bundle. The bail
message is counting taps that never occurred, because _cc_auto_stuck_tick was
called on ENTRY -- before the stability gate -- so every deferred tick was
charged to the tap budget.

Two safeguards then destroyed each other, in exact lockstep:
    tick 1  count=1  gate arms       (no tap)
    tick 2  count=2  hop 1/4         (no tap)
    tick 3  count=3  hop 2/4         (no tap)
    tick 4  count=4  hop 3/4         (no tap)
    tick 5  count=5 >= _CC_AUTO_STUCK_LIMIT -> BAIL
_CC_OPEN_HOP_GIVEUP is 4, so hop 4 -- the one that abandons the matcher and
taps the KNOWN-GOOD canonical -- needs tick 6 and is unreachable. Off by one,
with the bail always winning.

Why the matcher hops at all: the anchor is unreachable (reach=false len=-1),
so the CC teleport re-fires every few seconds and jogs the camera. (1164,382)
is 21px from the canonical (1185,387) -- the real button -- while (1051,531)
is down by the skill bar. The gate is right to distrust that, and its give-up
was the correct escape; it just never got there.

Fix: charge the stuck budget where the tap actually happens, after the gate.
It now counts taps instead of attempts, which is what its own message claims.

Verified by simulating the bundle's tick sequence:
    BEFORE  taps=[]   BAILED at tick 5 (no tap ever)   <- reproduces the bundle
    AFTER   taps=[5]  give-up fires and taps the canonical

Second-order fix: 0.5.125 treats these bails as evidence the game is dropping
taps, so phantom bails would have triggered spurious game restarts on a game
that was responding perfectly. Counting real taps removes that too.

   armed_age climbing, nothing ever pressed.

   finish_monster, or on a MAP CHANGE. A party WIPE kills nothing, and
   InfoDungeon.recover restores the SAME dungeon — so the flag latches True
   forever, and monsters_active is precisely the gate that makes bot.py stand
   down. Same shape as 0.5.119, where it locked the bot out of the entire red
   portal UI.

   guess — if monsters really are still up after the revive, the next spawn
   event sets the flag again within seconds, whereas a stale True never clears
   at all. Verified: clears on recover-SUCCEEDED, leaves the mid-wipe popup and
   the bare recover-CALLED alone.

   overlay plus the region banner on pure black, while the lua reported
   CC-FREEZE-DIAG idx=54 battleElapsed=142s monCount=18 and fired CC-RE-ENGAGE.

   nav-progress: the lua reports hero tiles changing, so there IS progress.
   liveness: the loop ticks. memory/taps: nothing wrong. The screen is the only

   hold, so a dim-but-real scene fails the mean test and a bright frame with a
   black border fails the fraction test. Sustained 90s before acting, since
   legitimate fades exist. 11/11 on every real frame we have (stuck, two

   CC, whereas a change to another map cannot -- a CC anchor exists on exactly
   one map. Re-entering the SAME map leaves the arm untouched. Verified on all

def _relaunch_guard_ok(history: deque) -> bool:
    """True iff firing one more relaunch right now stays under the cap."""
    now = time.monotonic()
    while history and (now - history[0]) > _RELAUNCH_GUARD_WINDOW_S:
        history.popleft()
    return len(history) < _RELAUNCH_GUARD_MAX


def _relaunch_game(adb: ADB, launch_activity: str) -> bool:
    """Fire `am start` against the game's main activity. Returns True on
    success. The lua-side cold-start init (bot_autopilot.lua:251) reads
    _bot_was_running_pre_crash on its own, so python's only job is to get
    the process up again - no python-side flag write needed."""
    try:
        subprocess.run(
            [adb.adb, "-s", adb.device, "shell",
             "am", "start", "-n", launch_activity],
            capture_output=True, timeout=15,
        )
        log.info("cold-start: am start %s fired", launch_activity)
        return True
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        log.warning("cold-start: am start timed out")
        return False
    except Exception as e:
        log.warning("cold-start: am start failed (%s)", e)
        return False


def _trim_game_memory(adb: "ADB", package: str) -> None:
    """v0.5.26: ask the game to release cached memory (Android onTrimMemory),
    a cheap periodic counter-pressure against the BlueStacks OOM leak. Does NOT
    free leaked-but-referenced memory, but reclaims cache so the OOM builds
    slower (extends time-between-crashes). Best-effort; errors are non-fatal."""
    try:
        subprocess.run(
            [adb.adb, "-s", adb.device, "shell",
             "am", "send-trim-memory", package, "RUNNING_CRITICAL"],
            capture_output=True, timeout=10,
        )
        log.info("mem-trim: send-trim-memory RUNNING_CRITICAL -> %s", package)
    except Exception as e:
        log.debug("mem-trim: failed (%s)", e)

ship 0.5.131 — a systematic audit instead of another one-off fix

Rather than chase the next report, I swept the whole codebase for the
failure SHAPES that produced this week's regressions. Five real defects,
each with field evidence, not speculation.

1. Cold-start relaunch was never verified (the 601s blind window).
   _relaunch_game returns True when the adb call did not THROW, not when
   the game started, and the caller latched crash_relaunch_fired on it.
   Bundle B39E3543: "am start fired" at 21:02:32, then NOTHING until the
   600s silent-stall at 21:12:48. That hole is the user's "never managed
   to get back in". The escalate-to-VM-restart ladder already existed and
   never ran, because a failed relaunch looked identical to a good one.
   Now verified with _wait_for_game_pid — the same check the stale-lua
   path has always done.

2. CC RUSH lottery rerolls counted as completed runs. A reroll enters a
   floor, rejects the chest and exits, and that exit is indistinguishable
   from a finished run at the counter edge. B39E3543: 51 "runs", 48
   lottery exits — 94% false. Corrupts max_runs (100 requested -> ~6 real)
   and would make the run-based refresh axis unsafe to re-enable. Also
   corrects the 0.5.81 docstring, which claimed the opposite.

3. auto_relic_busy could latch forever. It stands the ENTIRE main loop
   down and its only escapes were a lua callback and a map change; a
   dropped callback froze the bot on a game that was running fine, so
   silent-stall (which needs logcat SILENCE) stood down too. Measured in
   1123ccbot.log: 1 popup in 6 opened without closing. game_state already
   recorded auto_relic_busy_at and never read it — the timeout it was
   written for was never built. Built now, 60s.

4. cc_auto_step still starved the portal handlers. The 0.5.119 hoist put
   them above monsters_active but below the CC step, so a stuck CC still
   consumed every tick. A CC only exists on an akasa floor map, so the CC
   step is now skipped inside the portal outright — a second, independent
   brake alongside 0.5.130's map-change arm clear.

5. 15 lua markers could never reach bot.log, including AKASA-END and the
   SHOP-SKIP I shipped last week. Verified all 17 relay now.

Deliberately NOT changed: relic_popup_open has the same latch shape but
zero field occurrences and a working second escape, so it gets a note
rather than speculative code.

Verified: lottery suppression unit-tested against the real 48-reroll
sequence (0 counted, 48 suppressed, genuine runs still count); all 17

---
name: feedback-latch-needs-lease
description: Any flag set on a remote callback or an unverified action must have a timeout/verification, or it freezes the bot invisibly
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

A boolean that gates the bot into standing down, set by one event and
cleared only by a *correlated* second event, WILL eventually latch. Three
of the five 0.5.131 audit bugs were this exact shape:

- `auto_relic_busy` — stood the whole main loop down; cleared only by a lua
  onComplete/onClose or a map change. Measured 1-in-6 dropped callbacks in
  1123ccbot.log.
- `crash_relaunch_fired` — set from `_relaunch_game`, which returns True when
  the adb call did not THROW, not when the game started. See
  [[project-coldstart-relaunch-unverified]].
- `cc_auto_active` — cleared only by CC-AUTO-DONE, which never comes when a CC
  is abandoned. Fixed 0.5.130.

**Why:** these freeze the bot while the GAME stays healthy and chatty, so
silent-stall (which needs logcat SILENCE) stands down too. Nothing else can
see it. Same blind spot as [[project_game_progress_hang_luagetsize]].

**How to apply:** when adding a stand-down flag, add the lease in the same
commit — a timestamp + expiry, or verification that the action really
happened. A written-but-never-read `*_at` field is the tell that someone
intended a timeout and never built it (`auto_relic_busy_at` sat unread for
~50 releases). Prefer a self-expiring timestamp over a boolean: a stuck
boolean is the bug you are trying to prevent.
EOF
cat > "$M/feedback_synthetic_logcat_test_format.md" <<'EOF'
---
name: feedback-synthetic-logcat-test-format
description: Exact line format required for a synthetic logcat line to parse in game_state tests; wrong format silently reads as "marker unreachable"
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

`GameState._parse` needs BOTH:
1. the literal substring `[LUA-print]` (cheap pre-filter), and
2. `RE_DISPATCH = re.compile(r"\[LUA-print\]\s+(?:" + parts + ")")` — so the
   marker must follow `[LUA-print]` with only whitespace between. Any filler
   such as `[INFO] ` in between makes it NOT match.

Working test line:
`08-21 22:49:52.419 D/cocos2d-x debug info( 5912): [LUA-print] $$$ bot akasa-nav SHOP-SKIP cost=0`

Note the prefix is `akasa-nav`, not `akasa`, for the `andbg_kind` family.
`$$$ bot akasa CC-LOTTERY ...` is a DIFFERENT pattern.

**Why:** I got this wrong three separate ways in one session (missing
`[LUA-print]`, then an `[INFO]` filler, then `akasa` for `akasa-nav`). Each
time every marker came back "unreachable" and it looked like a real relay bug.
That is indistinguishable from the genuine defect in
[[feedback_marker_must_reach_botlog]], so it burns real time.

**How to apply:** before concluding a marker cannot reach bot.log, prove the
harness works by parsing a marker you KNOW is whitelisted (e.g. `PROBE`). If
that fails too, the harness is wrong, not the whitelist.
EOF
cat > "$M/project_coldstart_relaunch_unverified.md" <<'EOF'
---
name: project-coldstart-relaunch-unverified
description: "Restarted and never came back" = cold-start fired am start, never checked it worked, and went blind for 601s; fixed 0.5.131
metadata:

---

Bundle B39E3543 (0.5.129), the user's "CC rush ran for like 2 min then it
restarted the game and never managed to get back in":

```
21:02:01  black-screen watchdog: 99s -> force-stop   (90s threshold, my regression)
21:02:32  cold-start: am start ... fired
   ...    NOTHING. no logcat events at all.
21:12:48  silent-stall: no events for 601s -> force cold-start
21:13:33  game memory: 420 MB      <- only now is the game actually up
```

`_relaunch_game` returns True when the adb subprocess did not THROW — the
returncode and `am start`'s own "Error:" output are both discarded. The caller
then latched `crash_relaunch_fired = True`, so it never tried again.

The escalation ladder (2 failures in the guard window -> restart the BlueStacks
VM) already existed and was correct; it never ran because a failed relaunch was
indistinguishable from a successful one.

Fix 0.5.131: `_wait_for_game_pid` after `am start` (`FARMER_COLDSTART_VERIFY_S`,
30s). On failure, log and do NOT latch, so the existing ladder escalates.
The stale-lua path at bot.py:782 had ALWAYS verified this way — the crash path
just never got the same treatment.

Tell: `cold-start: am start returned but no <pkg> process after Ns`.
See [[feedback-latch-needs-lease]].
EOF
cat > "$M/project_lottery_rerolls_inflate_runs.md" <<'EOF'
---
name: project-lottery-rerolls-inflate-runs
description: CC RUSH lottery rerolls counted as completed runs (94% false in one bundle), corrupting max_runs and the run-based refresh axis; fixed 0.5.131
metadata:
  type: project
---

A CC RUSH lottery reroll enters a floor, rejects the chest and exits — and that
dungeon exit is indistinguishable from a finished run at bot.py's run-complete
edge. Bundle B39E3543: **51 "run complete" vs 48 lottery exits**, 20 of them
inside 3.5 minutes (one per ~10s).

Consequences: `max_runs` is corrupt (asking for 100 runs gives ~6 real ones),
the run number in the log is meaningless, and the run-based refresh axis is
unsafe — at 40 runs it restarted the game every ~7 min.

IMPORTANT NUANCE: the run axis was already defaulted OFF in **0.5.105**, so by
0.5.129 this was NOT what restarted users' games. I initially claimed it was and
had to correct myself — the restarts in B39E3543 came from the 90s black-screen
threshold (see [[project-coldstart-relaunch-unverified]]). This fix restores
counter correctness and makes the run axis safe to re-enable; it is not a
restart fix.

Also corrects the 0.5.81 `_proactive_refresh_due` docstring, which claimed rush
mode "barely ticks runs_completed (63 dungeon-exits but only 3 completed runs)".
The measurement says the opposite.

Fix: game_state records `cc_lottery_exit_at` on the lua's `CC-LOTTERY exit OK`
(MISS and exit OK pair 1:1, so keying on the exit counts each reroll once); the
run edge skips the increment within 30s. Timestamp, not a flag, so it cannot
latch. Tell: `CC RUSH: lottery reroll (not counted as a run; still N/inf)`.
EOF
